caption: The drawing depicts a single, urn-shaped object identified as a caster, rendered in graphite or pencil on a beige or light brown paper with visible darker stains and aging marks around the edges. The caster is approximately 5 inches tall as noted in the lower left corner and consists of a rounded base, a bulbous lower body with a slightly indented waist, and a cylindrical upper section that tapers into a dome-shaped perforated lid. The lid is topped with a small, sculpted finial. The perforations on the lid are regularly spaced, and the body of the caster is shaded to suggest a metallic or reflective surface. Handwritten text in the lower right corner identifies the object as “CASTER 18199.32 CASE #2” and is signed “Joseph M. Lisle.” The drawing is centered within a rectangular border, and beyond this border, stains and discolorations surround the main image.
title: Silver Caster
